profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between Quant Research and Analytics Delivery at a sell-side rates desk to align the handoff for a new macroeconomic-based no-arbitrage inflation model into the bank's pricing and risk stack before the quarterly model-risk committee. Context: the research team has finished a prototype that links inflation and nominal-rate dynamics to central-bank reaction functions, liquidity effects, and growth/inflation expectations, and the delivery team needs to package it for desk validation and pilot risk reporting. Agenda: confirm what the first calibration package includes, agree which market data snapshot will be used for validation, align how the model will be connected to the existing risk workflow, and clarify the first-release coverage for year-on-year inflation options. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on the deliverables, data basis, implementation path, and timeline for the pilot handoff.

members.name: Elena Rossi
members.expertise: Inflation derivatives modelling, affine term-structure methods, continuous-time macro-finance models, calibration design
members.background: Former academic economist turned front-office quant; she authored the internal note adapting a DSGE-inspired inflation framework into a separable no-arbitrage pricing model consistent with time-varying Hull-White nominal dynamics.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot to showcase the model's structural policy-scenario strengths without getting delayed by desk-specific edge cases, and she is trying to protect the research timeline by handing off something clean, defensible, and limited to standard conventions first.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'full curve calibration' for a first pilot, they mean the staged calibration to the liquid vanilla instruments used in the research note: nominal curve, nominal vol surface, and standard zero-coupon and year-on-year inflation quotes.
References to 'the example snapshot' point to the archived market dataset used in the published calibration example unless someone explicitly names a newer file date.
A 'risk run' for this model means a research-style scenario analysis where policy-rule and liquidity parameters are shocked directly, not the bank's overnight production VaR machinery.

Support for 'YoY options' in an initial release means standard annual year-on-year cap/floor structures under benchmark EUR inflation conventions, not every booked trade variant with stubs or interpolation quirks.

members.name: Daniel Brooks
members.expertise: Front-office pricing library integration, model onboarding, market data interfaces, validation workflows
members.background: He leads the team that turns quant prototypes into desk-usable services, coordinating with market data, risk technology, and model validation across rates and inflation products.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid a pilot that later needs rework from implementation gaps, so he is trying to fit the new model cleanly into existing production conventions and ensure the desk can use it on live books with minimal custom support.
hidden_assumptions: When research says a model is ready for 'full calibration,' that includes the broader set of desk-marked instruments and conventions needed for daily production use, not just the liquid calibration backbone.
A reference to 'the market snapshot from the example' naturally means the frozen validation snapshot in the shared onboarding folder, because that is the standard source used by implementation teams.

Putting a model into the 'risk run' means wiring it into the standard overnight risk engine and mapping its outputs into existing factor buckets rather than running a separate research scenario stack.
If a release claims 'YoY options support,' it should reprice the year-on-year option trades actually sitting on the desk, including off-cycle accruals, lags, and seasonality-handling variations.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'full curve calibration' package
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss delivering a 'full curve calibration' for the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a separable calibration across the standard liquid pillars from the research framework: nominal curve, nominal vol surface, zero-coupon inflation, and standard year-on-year inflation quotes, sufficient to demonstrate the model's consistency and closed forms.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means a desk-ready calibration package broad enough to support daily marks for the full production instrument set and conventions the inflation desk relies on, even if the model is only piloted initially.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds routine and well understood in quant onboarding discussions; because both expect staged rollout and both know the model is 'separable,' neither feels a need to enumerate the exact boundary of included instruments.

misalignment_points.topic: Which market data snapshot is 'the example'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to validate on 'the market snapshot from the example.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of the archived Bloomberg snapshot used in her research note's market calibration example, chosen because it illustrates taper-related policy effects clearly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the latest frozen validation snapshot in the shared implementation folder from last Friday, because onboarding workflows normally use the current official pack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe there is an obvious single 'example' dataset already circulating, and the phrase feels specific enough that neither asks for a date stamp or file name.

misalignment_points.topic: How the model will be 'plugged into the risk run'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the model should be 'plugged into the risk run' before committee review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena expects a research-style scenario engine where the central-bank reaction-function parameters, liquidity factor, and inflation-growth expectation channels are shocked directly to show structural policy sensitivities.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel expects to integrate the model into the standard overnight risk infrastructure, approximating its impact through existing rates and inflation factor mappings and reporting conventions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the business purpose—showing risk impact before committee—and 'risk run' is a common catch-all phrase; the different execution methods are second-order enough that each assumes the other's workflow is the conventional one.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included under 'YoY options support'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both confirm that 'YoY options support' is in scope for the first drop.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the closed-form pricing for standard annual year-on-year inflation caps/floors under the benchmark index lag and convention embedded in the model note.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the implementation should handle the year-on-year option structures the desk actually books, including irregular periods, interpolation, and seasonality choices that sit around the standard formula.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both know the model already has a closed-form YoY option result, the statement 'support is in scope' sounds complete; neither thinks to separate core formula availability from operational trade-convention coverage.
